title: Watch: Freddie Freeman falls down Royals dugout steps, Dodgers 'dodge' bullet
description: Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Freddie Freeman fell down dugout steps, resulting in soreness throughout his body in a win over the Kansas City Royals.
fullText:
Aug. 13 (UPI) -- Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Freddie Freeman fell down dugout steps, resulting in soreness throughout his body in a win over the Kansas City Royals.

The tumble occurred in the top of the eighth inning of the 4-2 victory Wednesday in Los Angeles. Freeman said he felt soreness in his knees, shoulder, hand and wrist, but did not break any bones.

"I didn't hit my head, so that was the key part," Freeman told reporters.

Freeman said he used the cold tub and was in "good spirits" during his postgame news conference. He said he is hopeful to play Thursday at Dodger Stadium.

"I'm OK," said Freeman, who said everything on his right side is sore. "This one's not my ankle, so I should be OK."

The 10-time All-Star went 1 for 2 with a walk and a strikeout in the win. The Dodgers trailed twice through the first 2 1/2 innings, with the Royals taking two one-run leads. They took a 3-2 edge off a 397-foot, two-run homer from Shohei Ohtani and never looked back. Catcher Hunter Feduccia provided insurance with a 402-foot solo shot in the fourth.

Royals pinch hitter John Rave started the eighth with a fly out to right fielder Kyle Tucker. Designated hitter Carter Jensen reached base through a fielding error in the next at-bat.

Left fielder Isaac Collins then walked to the plate with two outs. He earned a 2-1 lead in the count against Dodgers relief pitcher Landon Knack. The right-handed pitcher then tossed in a 93-mph fastball, which Collins sliced into foul territory near first base.

Freeman pursued the ball and hovered toward the dugout. He then took a long step with his left foot, but fell down the steps instead of snagging the final out of the inning. The Dodgers star, who said he was attempting to lean on the dugout fence, told reporters that he misjudged its location. Royals players and coaches checked on Freeman before he got up and left the dugout.

Pinch hitter Michal Massey struck out in the next exchange, ending the half inning.

Freeman, who was set to lead off the bottom of the eighth, was replaced by Tommy Edman. The 17-year veteran said he experienced a similar fall about 10 years ago.

"I think that we really dodged a bullet," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Very scary visually. ... For right now, he's in good spirits, which I think is a good sign. Just kind of total body soreness. He'll be day-to-day."

Shohei flips the script! pic.twitter.com/eVrqvcBmMs— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) August 13, 2026

Freeman already was set to have Friday off. He said he did not undergo X-ray scans Wednesday night. Roberts said he doesn't plan to promote an minor league players in the wake of Freeman's fall.

Ohtani went 2 for 4 with two RBIs, a run scored and a strikeout. Shortstop Mookie Betts also homered in the victory. Dodgers starter Eric Lauer allowed four hits and two runs, including one earned, over 6 1/3 innings to improve to 7-6 this season.

Freeman hit a team-high .306 with 15 home runs and 57 RBIs through 118 games this season.

The Dodgers (73-48), who were on a seven-game losing skid earlier this month, are now on a three-game winning streak. They hold an 8.5-game lead on the San Diego Padres (65-57), who sit in second place in the National League West.

The Dodgers will host the Milwaukee Brewers, who own the best record in the National League (74-47), at 10:10 p.m. EDT Thursday in Los Angeles.

title: Celtic Eye Summer Move For This Veteran Newcastle United Custodian: Should He Replace Sinisalo As The Hoops ‘Number 1’?
description: If a recent report from The Daily Mail (as cited by The Daily Express) is believed to be true, Celtic are keeping close tabs on Nick Pope ahead of a potential summer move. But they are not alone in th...
fullText:
If a recent report from The Daily Mail (as cited by The Daily Express) is believed to be true, Celtic are keeping close tabs on Nick Pope ahead of a potential summer move. But they are not alone in the race, with Premier League newcomers  Ipswich Town also eyeing a move for the Newcastle United goalkeeper.

The 34-year-old England international progressed through Ipswich Town's academy ranks before leaving his boyhood side for non-league outfit Bury Town. Charlton secured his services in the summer of 2011; however, he was primarily loaned out to Harrow Borough, Welling United, Cambridge United, Aldershot Town, York City and Bury in the lower leagues to gain first-team experience. An impressive 2015-16 campaign for the Addicks in the Championship earned him a £1.1m transfer to then newly-promoted Premier League outfit Burnley.

After spending the first season as the understudy to Tom Heaton, Pope cemented a starting status between the sticks and went on to feature 155 times for the Clarets before securing a £10m switch to the Magpies in 2022. Despite being the preferred option in the last line of defence, the Three Lions veteran has struggled at times due to form and fitness reasons. Newcastle have splashed a combined fee of around £45m for Lukáš Horníček and Ewen Jaouen, respectively, from Braga and Reims, thus making him surplus to requirements under new boss Matthias Jaissle.

LONDON, ENGLAND – FEBRUARY 10: Nick Pope of Newcastle United punches the ball during the Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on February 10, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

Celtic have made an electrifying start to their Premiership title defence with back-to-back wins against Dundee and Kilmarnock. They have opted for quality over quantity, with Camilo Duran and Kasper Høgh being the only arrivals so far this window. Martin O'Neill has banked on Viljami Sinisalo since Kasper Schmeichel's season-ending shoulder injury, which eventually forced the Dane to retire upon the closure of the previous campaign.

Although the Finnish shot-stopper has retained the 'number 1' spot, the Celts have opted for an experienced, established figure over a younger alternative in the recent past. Schmeichel was brought in as a like-for-like replacement for Joe Hart, and it remains to be seen whether they follow a similar strategy before the window is slammed shut.

Pope might prefer a return to his hometown club, but a move north of the border would see him contest for silverware rather than engage in a survival battle. Assured minutes in Europe should further fascinate him to ply his trade in Glasgow, as his expertise in goal could earn him the first-choice status for at least a couple of seasons ahead of Sinisalo.

title: How a roster loophole could solve Steelers' four-QB dilemma
description: By utilizing a practice squad loophole with veteran Mason Rudolph, the Pittsburgh Steelers can retain Will Howard and Drew Allar on the roster.
fullText:
As the Pittsburgh Steelers navigate a delicate quarterback puzzle behind starter Aaron Rodgers, head coach Mike McCarthy faces a classic 53-man roster crunch.

Carrying four quarterbacks: Rodgers, veteran Mason Rudolph, second-year passer Will Howard, and third-round rookie Drew Allar, is virtually unheard of in modern NFL roster construction. However, an intricate roster loophole involving Rudolph's status as a "vested veteran" could offer Pittsburgh an ideal strategic compromise to keep everyone.

Because Rudolph possesses at least four accrued NFL seasons, he is legally exempt from the league's waiver wire system if released. While non-vested young prospects like Howard or Allar would be exposed to waiver claims from 31 other teams, Rudolph immediately becomes an unrestricted free agent who can re-sign on his own terms.

During a recent segment on "PFT Live," NFL analyst Mike Florio broke down how Pittsburgh could exploit this procedural mechanism to protect its entire quarterback room:

"The veteran, the vested veteran gets cut, doesn't have to sign through waivers, hangs around, re-signs to the roster, signs to the practice squad. They could put Mason Rudolph on the practice squad, elevate him to the active roster, send him back down, do that a few weeks, and then do it all over again, release him from the roster," explained Florio.

Under NFL practice squad regulations, teams can elevate a veteran player up to three times per season without signing them to the active 53-man list. By executing a handshake agreement with Rudolph, Pittsburgh could temporarily release him at final roster cutdowns, stash him on the practice squad, and promote him on game days when needed.

This clever procedural maneuvering would allow the Steelers to retain their high-upside developmental assets on the 53-man roster while preserving Rudolph's essential veteran presence behind Rodgers without burning a valuable position spot. While reliant on mutual trust and personal flexibility, it provides Pittsburgh a unique mechanism to solve an otherwise difficult numbers game.

title: 49ers may want to sign RB as injuries mount before preseason opener
description: A trio of veteran RBs were all at the San Francisco 49ers facility for workouts or visits leading up to their preseason opener.
fullText:
The San Francisco 49ers brought in outside help at running back Monday, working out veterans Nyheim Miller-Hines and Zamir White while also hosting Blake Watson on a visit, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The timing tracks with San Francisco's depth chart, which has thinned out fast heading into a joint practice and Thursday's preseason game. Christian McCaffrey sat out Monday's practice with tightness, though the team said the star back is fine. Rookie Jordan James is dealing with a broken rib. Isaac Guerendo is also banged up, and Kaelon Black is nursing a minor injury of his own. With four backs compromised in some form, the Niners needed bodies to get through a physical week of practice against another team's defense.

None of the players who worked out are household names, but each has NFL mileage. Miller-Hines, a fourth-round pick by the Colts in 2018, spent five seasons in Indianapolis and has bounced through stops with the Bills, Browns, the Chargers and Saints since tearing his ACL in a 2023 offseason accident. White, a 2022 fourth-rounder out of Georgia, was the Raiders' lead back for stretches before falling out of the Raiders' rotation last season. Watson, an undrafted free agent out of Memphis who ran an unofficial 4.39-second 40 at his pro day, made the Broncos' initial 53-man roster in 2024 and has bounced between the Broncos' active roster and practice squad since.

San Francisco hasn't announced any signings, but adding a body or two before Thursday's game would hardly be a surprise given the state of the room. It's also a reminder of how quickly joint practices can get complicated for the 49ers — in 2024, the team was forced to scrap its joint sessions with the Saints due to a bevy of injuries. ESPN's Nick Wagoner reported the 49ers were concerned they wouldn't have enough players healthy to even practice.

title: Biden-world veteran issues stark warning about Abdul El-Sayed as he crosses party lines
description: Michael LaRosa invoked his best friend's mother, who died jumping from the World Trade Center on 9/11, in his sharp rebuke of Abdul El-Sayed.
fullText:
Former Jill Biden press secretary Michael LaRosa said he won't support Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, citing the candidate's refusal to distance himself from far-left streamer Hasan Piker over his past remarks about the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks.

LaRosa, who served as press secretary to former first lady Jill Biden, made the unusually sharp break with his party in a post responding to reports that he was supporting Republican Mike Rogers over El-Sayed.

At the center of LaRosa's criticism is El-Sayed's association with Piker, who drew widespread condemnation after saying during a 2019 livestream that "America deserved 9/11."

El-sayed's Socialist Allies Reject Gop Claims About Dems Embracing The Far Left

El-Sayed has campaigned alongside Piker and, when pressed about the remark, has argued that appearing with the streamer does not mean he endorses everything Piker has said.

For LaRosa, the controversy is deeply personal. He said the mother of his best friend died on Sept. 11 after jumping from the 95th floor of the World Trade Center rather than remain inside the burning building.

"I won't defend or support anyone who is too cowardly to stand up to extremists who think the mother of my best friend, who jumped from 95 stories because the alternative was worse, deserved what happened to her," LaRosa wrote. "Her only crime was showing up to work that morning."

Hasan Piker Calls For Democrats Who Oppose Abdul El-sayed To Be 'Punished'

LaRosa concluded by accusing El-Sayed of refusing to stand up to "the guy who says she 'deserved' what she got that morning she showed up for work."

LaRosa's rebuke is about more than one Democrat refusing to back another.

It highlights a growing fault line within the party over extremism and the boundaries of acceptable political rhetoric. Those divisions could ultimately push some longtime Democrats across the aisle in consequential races.

That dynamic could prove particularly consequential in Michigan, where the Senate contest could help shape the balance of power in Washington and even a small erosion of Democratic support could matter.

title: This veteran to arrive at Newcastle United and be the positive influence needed?
description: Sometimes, experience is just as valuable as youth — and Newcastle United could be about to find that out. After weeks of uncertainty, ins and outs, rumours and endless speculation, things are finally beginning to settle down at Newcastle United.
fullText:
Sometimes, experience is just as valuable as youth — and Newcastle United could be about to find that out.

After weeks of uncertainty, ins and outs, rumours and endless speculation, things are finally beginning to settle down at Newcastle United.

There are fresh faces through the door, players returning from the World Cup, and a new manager and coaching staff putting the squad through its paces in La Manga, Spain.

From what I have seen of the early training sessions, the intensity is certainly there. Throw in temperatures of 30-plus degrees and the lads are going to know they have been working hard this week!

One thing that particularly pleased me was the apparent passion on show. Both the players and coaching staff looked fully engaged, and there seemed to be a real intensity about the sessions.

Of course, training is one thing — now we need to see that same attitude and commitment transferred onto the pitch when it really matters.

And then there is Pierre-Emile Højbjerg.

Reports linking the 31-year-old with a move to Newcastle have raised more than a few eyebrows, with a fee of around £10m-£15m being bandied about.

Personally, I don't see what all the fuss is about.

In fact, I think it could be a very sensible piece of business.

Højbjerg is a seasoned Premier League player with considerable experience, and at around £10m-£15m, he certainly wouldn't break the bank. More importantly, he could bring somethingNewcastle United will need in abundance — experience.

With several young players coming into the squad, having an experienced head in the dressing room could prove invaluable. Højbjerg knows the Premier League, understands the demands of playing at the highest level and, importantly, has been there before.

Sometimes the value of a player cannot simply be measured by goals, assists or statistics.

It can be measured by what happens around him.

The influence he has on younger players. The standards he sets in training. The calmness he brings when things aren't going according to plan. The voice in the dressing room when the pressure starts to build.

We have already seen how important that kind of experience can be.

Our noisy neighbours down the road benefited considerably from the addition of Granit Xhaka, while Newcastle themselves saw the impact Kieran Trippier made when he arrived at St James' Park.

Trippier wasn't just a footballer. He brought leadership, experience and standards — qualities that had a positive influence on those around him.

That kind of influence should never be underestimated.

So, while some supporters may question whether Højbjerg is the right age or whether the money would be better spent elsewhere, I would be more than happy to see him arrive on Tyneside.

Newcastle United have plenty of young talent. What they also need is the experience to help that talent flourish.

If Højbjerg can provide that, then perhaps this is one transfer we shouldn't be scoffing at.

Instead, we should be asking whether another experienced head could be exactly what this new-look Newcastle United needs.

Canucks Should Bring In This UFA Goalie Amid Demko Uncertainty
description: The Vancouver Canucks should look into bringing in this veteran netminder, amid the likelihood of an experiment this upcoming season. The post Canucks Should Bring In This UFA Goalie Amid Demko Uncertainty appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Vancouver Canucks will likely need to conduct a bit of an experiment in 2026-27. The uncertainty surrounding Thatcher Demko's health could very well prompt the organization to carry three goalies.

Yes, the Canucks are rebuilding. But just because they're rebuilding it doesn't mean the team should throw a Zamboni driver out there if and when Demko goes down.

And that's the thing. There's no real telling when Demko could go down. The numbers have shown that Demko typically goes down after seven starts or so. Even if Demko remained fully healthy this season, the Canucks will have to be very careful with his workload.

That's why the Canucks will need a third goalie. The easiest and most cost-effective option is to call someone up from Abbotsford. That could mean Nikita Tolopilo getting a fair number of starts.

But would the organization be better off keeping Tolopilo in the press box when Demko plays? Or would the team be better served by Tolopilo getting regular reps in Abbotsford?

That's where a veteran goalie like Ingram comes into the mix. Ingram can hang around as the backup to Kevin Lankinen on the nights Demko doesn't even dress.

That's another thing. The Canucks, in order to manage Demko's workload, shouldn't even dress him on nights he doesn't play. That's why a tandem like Lankinen and Ingram on Demko's nights off would give the team a better chance to win and keep Demko healthy.

The most complex situation for the Canucks will be handling back-to-back sets this upcoming season. Since starting Demko in one leg and then having him back up the next night might be a bit much, Manny Malhotra can let Demko rest on consecutive nights, especially on the road.

Back-to-back sets away from Vancouver could prove especially challenging for Demko. So, rolling with Lankinen and Ingram on the road would help Demko avoid injury as much as possible.

At home, Demko could get one leg, with either Lankinen or Ingram starting the other. If such a rotation sounds weird, it looks to be the next big trend in the NHL, particularly with the season now moving to 84 games.

Canucks Could Have Interesting Comp for Petterson Trade

The Canucks already made a risky bet in signing Demko to the extension they did. Since no one will be taking the contract off their hands, the best thing the organization can do is just give Demko the best possible shot at succeeding.

That's why the Canucks can't suddenly get cheap with goaltending. The team will need to have stability in the crease, especially with a younger defense emerging around them. The last thing Vancouver should be looking at is something like an inexperienced goalie giving up three goals on five shots in the first period.

Having a solid netminder behind the likes of Zeev Buium and Tom Willander will be crucial in building their confidence as they grow into bona fide NHL defensemen. So, even if Ingram costs something like $3 million on a one-year deal, it's an investment the team must make in helping its young D core develop.

title: Bruins Could Get Some More Beef on D With This Vet
description: The Boston Bruins could get some more beef on the blue line with this veteran D-man, given the opponents in the East. The post Bruins Could Get Some More Beef on D With This Vet appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Boston Bruins have had another relatively quiet offseason. In a way, remaining quiet is better than making questionable decisions. But as the rest of the Atlantic Division gears up for a big season, Don Sweeney can't afford to sit on his hands.

Fortunately, there's an interesting UFA option out there that could help add some more beef to the Bruins' lineup. That option is Logan Stanley.

The 6'7" 230-pound blueliner could very well give the Bruins a meaner edge heading into this season. That's something crucial when facing some of the more belligerent opponents like the Tampa Bay Lightning and Florida Panthers.

Adding Stanley should help solidify the bottom four, particularly with the departure of Andrew Peeke this summer. Peeke was mostly a defensive defenseman, something that all teams need to have in their bottom four.

Stanley brings that. He delivers decent if unspectacular play. His physicality is an asset, ensuring that the opposition remains honest.

The only question mark would be the terms of a deal for Stanley. The veteran blueliner is still 28 and likely looking for a multi-year deal. And that's just the thing. The Bruins might not be willing to commit beyond a one or two-year deal.

But there might be a way that the Bruins could bring Stanley in without breaking the bank.

The Bruins could take a shot on Stanley by signing him to a one-year, show-me deal. So, something along the lines of a $4 million cap hit, which might seem a bit onerous for a bottom-pairing defenseman, could make sense.

The deal could be part of a broader promise by the organization. If Stanley fits, the two sides could work out a contract extension. If he doesn't somehow fit in, he could be another NHL trade deadline piece to move.

Sure, the Bruins wouldn't get much for him at the deadline. But the club could allow Stanley to get another shot much like the Winnipeg Jets did this past season by sending him to the Buffalo Sabres.

Bruins Should Take Flyer on Hurricanes' Beleaguered Center

The prospect of rolling out Nikita Zadorov and Logan Stanley one after the other should be tantalizing to Bruins fans. The bruising, if not necessarily flashy play could help offset some of the apparent lack of offensive punch Boston shows.

The Bruins aren't built to win games by outscoring opponents. The game plan should once again focus on buying David Pastrnak enough time to bust games wide open.

And that's precisely what Stanley helps accomplish.

It's unclear if the Bruins would be willing to meet Stanley's contract demands. But if there's a way to work something out, the Bruins would be remiss if they didn't at least kick the tires on the hulking blueliner.

The Bruins need every edge they can get. And if it comes in a massive package, all the better. The Atlantic Division playoff race should be airtight. That's why having strong reinforcements could make a massive difference in 2026-27.

title: Democratic strategist James Carville says he could become a Republican under one major condition
description: Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville revealed the only hypothetical scenario in which he'd join the Republican Party as Hasan Piker and democratic socialists gain ground.
fullText:
Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville told Fox News Digital Thursday there is only one unlikely scenario in which he would actually join the Republican Party.

Posed with a hypothetical where Republicans had the policies of former President Bill Clinton from the 1990s and the Democratic Party fully embraced socialism, Carville said, "That's a fantasy, OK, but, yeah, hypothetically, if I — hypothetically I could fly to the moon — it's about the same chance that that happens.

"Well, if the Democrats went crazy and the Republicans went sane, then I probably would be a Republican," he added. "But I don't see any evidence that there's any possibility that the latter could happen.

"I think it's more likely than not that the Democrats embrace sanity," Carville continued, saying the party's direction will be determined by Democratic primary voters.

Hasan Piker's Defense Of Hamas Having 'Right To Resist Militarily' Draws Condemnation From Human Rights Groups

In recent months, there has been a rising faction of far-left Democratic candidates in multiple states to the point Carville has suggested there be a schism to keep them out of power.

Hasan Piker, a self-described socialist streamer who campaigned with Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, has emerged as a leading voice on the left as democratic socialists gain ground in elections across the country.

Piker is known for far-left rhetoric, including previously saying "America deserved 9/11." After widespread criticism, Piker said in an interview he "obviously" did not mean America deserved the attacks and defended the viral quote as a critique of U.S. foreign policy.

"I am not going to be in the same party with Hasan Piker," Carville said recently on Fox News' "The Sunday Briefing." "If he becomes a force in a Democratic Party, I'm out of here. I have no intention of ever being in the same political party with that guy."

Speaking to Fox News Digital on Thursday, Carville addressed what would happen if the socialist faction took over the Democratic Party.

"That probably would result in some kind of schism in the party," he reiterated. "I'm going to let Democratic voters determine the direction that party goes in, and if it goes in the direction — which I'm pretty confident it won't — but if it goes in that direction, then I'm going to be 82, OK, fine, go ahead, but not with me.

"Until Democratic voters choose the direction of the party, I'll try to do all I can to help them make the right choice, in my opinion."

John Fetterman Makes It 'Very Clear' That He's 'Not Going To Be A Republican' Despite Dem Backlash

Carville's threat to leave the Democratic Party has been mocked by its progressive wing.

"Now James Carville is talking about leaving the party," Piker said during a recent video appearance with El-Sayed. "We got [Pennsylvania Sen.] John Fetterman, James Carville fantasizing about leaving the party. I'm like, 'You're sweetening the deal.' That was really interesting."

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., has also stood by Piker after Carville's warning.

"Well, that's not much of a choice," Sanders said of choosing between Piker and Carville. "If Mr. Carville doesn't want to be in my party, the party that I belong to, that Piker, that El-Sayed belongs to, he can start his own party."

title: Browns’ Shedeur Sanders ranked as the worst veteran QB in the NFL; key reasons revealed
description: Cleveland Browns’ presumed QB1 Shedeur Sanders was ranked 35th out of the 35 eligible veteran QBs coming into the 2026-27 NFL season. Sanders had to fight his way to earn a starting role as the Browns’ QB over Dillon Gabriel last season, with this season’s battle also including veteran DeShaun Watson.
fullText:
Cleveland Browns' presumed QB1 Shedeur Sanders was ranked 35th out of the 35 eligible veteran QBs coming into the 2026-27 NFL season.

Sanders had to fight his way to earn a starting role as the Browns' QB over Dillon Gabriel last season, with this season's battle also including veteran DeShaun Watson.

Unfortunately, Sanders isn't going to enter next season as a rated QB, with executives and coaches clearly carrying a low opinion of the 24-year-old.

The Athletic's tier list survey of all 35 eligible veteran QBs saw Sanders rank dead-last, with some scathing comments from the respondents.

"He's inaccurate at all three levels," an exec said. "I can't tell if he is going to get better, but there's a huge gap between him and competent QB play."

"He's not an on-time player, can't really read through the coverages, is a little bit heavy-footed," one coordinator said. "He is thicker and harder to tackle than expected, but you shouldn't lose to him."

"I'd sleep like a baby if I got to play him every week," one defensive coordinator said.

fullText:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — With the Milwaukee Brewers' trade-deadline acquisition of veteran starter Dustin May, rookie right-hander Brandon Sproat became the odd man out of the rotation.

Sproat, who appeared in 21 games for Milwaukee, including 19 starts, was optioned Tuesday to Triple-A Nashville one day after another inconsistent start.

May, acquired from the Cardinals on Monday along with reliever JoJo Romero, is scheduled to start Thursday for Milwaukee in the series finale against Pittsburgh. Left-hander Kyle Harrison, on the injured list since July 9, also is scheduled to return and start Wednesday.

The 25-year-old Sproat, acquired from the Mets in the offseason trade for Freddy Peralta, is 3-7 with a 5.27 ERA for Milwaukee. He has not won in five starts since his last victory on June 30.

"I think you look at it at face value. It wasn't a foregone conclusion," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said before Tuesday's game. "It's really about what's best for the player and what's best for the team."

Sproat took the loss Monday in a 4-3 defeat in the series opener against the Pirates, allowing four runs on five hits in three-plus innings. He was removed after throwing consecutive wild pitches following a leadoff single in the fourth.

Sproat has struck out 100 in 95 2/3 innings with the Brewers. But he walked 48, hit nine batters and threw nine wild pitches.

"The free bases, the wild pitches, the walks, hit by pitches, has got to stop," Murphy said. "You can't pitch in the big leagues like that."

May was 5-7 with a 4.38 ERA in 21 starts with St. Louis, including 0-1 with a 4.62 ERA in six July starts.

The Brewers also optioned reliever Garrett Stallings to Nashville on Tuesday. In addition to getting Romero, Milwaukee also acquired reliever Antonio Senzatela from Colorado on Monday.

fullText:
MIAMI GARDENS — Confidence is a helluva thing. If you have it, you can move mountains. If you don’t have it, you’ll never move defensive tackles. This is what brings us around to Miami Dolphins right guard Jonah Savaiinaea, who had spirited battles with veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler in Monday’s practice.

A year ago, as an out-of-position rookie left guard, Savaiinaea, the 2025 second-round pick, lost his confidence. Playing left guard in the NFL, instead of right guard, the position he played in college, resulted in Savaiinaea thinking instead of playing freely. It slowed him down. He became nervous. And he was way too hard on himself when he made mistakes. It was a weekslong downward spiral. A loss of confidence is a big reason why Savaiinaea was rated as one of the NFL’s worst guards by Pro Football Focus.

This season, Savaiianea is trying to rebuild his confidence. So are the the Dolphins. They’re on an all-out assault to bring Savaiinaea back from the dark side.

“I don’t want to hear any more about Jonah last year just because it’s over,” coach Jeff Hafley said. “Let’s judge Jonah on everything that he’s doing today, moving forward and see how he does.”

It remains to be seen whether this experiment will be successful. After all, this is the NFL. Every story doesn’t have a happy ending.

But Savaiinaea is personable, upbeat and positive so you hope he does well this season and beyond.

Still, this is an uphill battle.

Savaiinaea is viewed as the weak link on this offensive line. He’s not especially good against the run or pass, and he hasn’t displayed much physicality. The interesting thing is that the latter might be the biggest issue considering Hafley wants to have a physical team that’s strong in the trenches. You can teach run or pass blocking. It’s tougher to teach physicality.

This is where Savaiinaea’s mental reckoning could save his job as well as the Dolphins’ offensive line.

Savaiinaea is trying to make changes.

“It comes all in the mind,” he said. “I have the physical attributes to go out there and become a professional football player, but at the end of the day, it’s all about how you attack everything mentally. … I’m a different person as far as mentally.”

Savaiinaea actually started this process late last season.

“Towards the end of the year, I told myself, ‘I’m on myself too much, so why not take it easy on yourself?’ ” he said.

There are other things that Savaiinaea did to flip the script from last season.

He switched to No. 71, the number he wore in college and high school, ditching No. 72, which he wore last season.

“I want to bring that back and I want to get back to that kind of a reset mode and start to be myself again,” he said.

Savaiinaea did good work Monday, and has been fairly reliable through five days of training camp. He also did good work against defensive tackle Kenneth Grant on Monday in both 1 on 1s and 11 on 11s. Yes, there was a play in which defensive tackle Zeek Biggers knocked Savaiinaea on his backside in the final session of 11 on 11, but he didn’t threaten quarterback Malik Willis.

All things considered, Savaiinaea has shown improvement from a year ago. He attributes it mostly to a change between the ears.

“It’s how I approach my work,” he said. “Nothing changed because the side switched or the number switched. I don’t think so. I feel as if I approach this game like I’m coming there to move somebody out of there and protect Malik behind there, I feel like I’m going to be successful in this league.”

title: Could Tre'Davious White be a smart veteran addition for the Bucs?
description: Tre'Davious White remains unsigned and the Bucs could use more help in the secondary, so does a signing make sense?
fullText:
Outside of Zyon McCollum, Tampa Bay is relying on several young defensive backs to play meaningful snaps this season. While rookies and second-year players have flashed throughout camp, adding another proven veteran before Week 1 could still be a wise move. One player who stands out as a potential fit is former All-Pro cornerback Tre'Davious White.

White is no longer the player who was once considered one of the NFL's premier shutdown corners, but that doesn't mean he can't still provide value. After battling multiple major injuries over the last several seasons, including a torn ACL and Achilles injury, White has struggled to recapture the elite form that made him a two-time Pro Bowler. Those setbacks have understandably impacted both his availability and consistency. But that's exactly why he could be an affordable option this late in the offseason.

Todd Bowles has never been afraid to lean on experienced defensive backs, particularly those who have proven they can thrive in man coverage. While White may have lost a step athletically, his instincts, football IQ, and understanding of route concepts remain strengths. Veteran corners often make up for diminished speed with anticipation, positioning, and technique, and White has years of experience doing just that.

The Buccaneers also wouldn't need him to be the player he was in Buffalo.

Instead, he could serve as an experienced rotational corner, provide quality depth in case injuries strike, and mentor a young secondary that features several players still learning the real speed of the NFL game. There's little downside to bringing in a player with White's résumé on the right contract. If he returns to even a fraction of his previous Pro Bowl level, Tampa Bay could have one of the better value signings of the late offseason. If not, the financial commitment would likely be minimal.

White could help bridge the gap that is starters with experience and then the drop off to two sophomores still trying to find their footing in a complex defense, especially with Benjamin Morrison still struggling with injuries. Having the option to ease into younger corners instead of trial by fire allows for flexibility, one of Todd Bowles' biggest strengths. If Tampa Bay wants to fully resolve its woes of last season, White could be the final depth piece.

title: Bears Teammates Highlight Garrett Bradbury's Communication Skills in Camp
description: Following Drew Dalman’s retirement, veteran center Garrett Bradbury has impressed teammates with a seamless transition, providing the veteran leadership and vocal presence for the Chicago Bears' offensive line.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears finally had stable play from the center position last season.

Drew Dalman played every offensive snap and earned himself a Pro Bowl nod. After years of instability on the interior spot of the offensive line, there was finally consistency.

Dalman retired in March, and the Bears quickly traded for New England Patriots center Garrett Bradbury. The veteran offensive lineman has seven years of NFL experience and 105 starts to his name.

Although he's the new guy on the Bears' O-line, his teammates haven't noticed a drop off in the operation of head coach Ben Johnson's offense.

"I think we were all a little, you know, you don't know how it's going to go, especially when we lose somebody like Drew, who's, you know, kind of that captain of the offensive line there communication wise," Bears tight end Cole Kmet said. "But, I mean, with Garrett, it really has been flawless so far, and I know we haven't had pads on from a physicality standpoint, but, you know, you talked about communication in the walkthroughs that we've had, and in practice, things have been really clear, concise, and I feel like when I've been out there, especially in the run game and the pass pro, things have been really clear. And I think we've had great understanding with one another, so yeah, it's a good unit up front for sure."

Braxton Jones is currently in a competition for the starting left tackle position, but he's also noticed the cohesion he's felt with Bradbury playing with the starting unit.

"I mean, Garrett's jumped right in," Jones said. "He's, I mean, it's almost, it's weird like, you know, shoutout to Drew Dalman and everything he did, but, you know, Garrett jumped right in and has done a great job. It's like, you know, the same thing, their communication is great. And, you know, obvioulsy Garrett's a hell of a player himself, so it's been great and the continuity going forward. We're all a brotherhood. We all have a good time, but whe it's ready to, you know, get that work in, we're all getting that work in. So, it's just a great group to be around.

Caleb Williams is now playing with his third center in the last three years. The center and quarterback relationship is an important one for any offense. After last Wednesday's training camp practice, he mentioned that there was a slight miscommunication between the two.

Training camp is the time to address those miscues, as the Bears' quarterback is looking for perfection on game days.

Garrett doesn't have to be perfect -- or Dalman -- but he does need to provide a stable presence at the center position for this Bears offense to reach its next level.

The Chicago Cubs spent the days leading up to the MLB trade deadline searching for a starting pitcher capable of making a difference in October.

The players heading back to Toronto were not immediately revealed.

The move gives the Cubs an experienced arm for the stretch run after the organization made upgrading its rotation a deadline priority. Although Gausman has not produced his best numbers this season, his track record and ability to miss bats make him a potentially significant addition.

Those numbers may not immediately jump off the page, but Gausman has shown encouraging signs recently. The 35-year-old allowed only one earned run over 5.2 innings against the St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday. He surrendered nine hits but avoided major damage, issuing one walk and striking out four in Toronto’s 5-1 victory.

Gausman also worked six innings against the Boston Red Sox in his previous start, allowing three earned runs while striking out six. Across his final two appearances for the Blue Jays, he recorded a 3.09 ERA with 10 strikeouts and only two walks in 11.2 innings. He joins Chicago with 385 major league appearances, including 345 starts. The two-time All-Star has compiled 2,081 strikeouts across more than 2,000 career innings while pitching for the Baltimore Orioles, Atlanta Braves, Cincinnati Reds, San Francisco Giants and Blue Jays.

Gausman also has experience on the postseason stage. He has appeared in 10 playoff games during his career, including eight starts.

The Cubs entered Sunday with a 61-51 record after a 2-1 loss to the New York Yankees. They remain firmly in the National League playoff race but needed another reliable starter to strengthen their chances of making a deep run.

Gausman gives Chicago a veteran who can absorb innings, generate strikeouts and potentially start an important postseason game.

He also arrives with another year remaining on the five-year, $110 million contract he signed with Toronto before the 2022 season. Gausman is scheduled to earn $23 million in 2027, meaning this is more than a short-term rental for the Cubs.

For the Blue Jays, the trade signals a different direction. Toronto fell to 52-60 with Saturday’s loss to St. Louis and entered Sunday 13.5 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East.

Rather than holding onto Gausman for another season, the Blue Jays elected to move one of their most accomplished starters and add to their future.

The full return will ultimately help determine how the trade is evaluated. For now, however, the immediate message is clear: The Cubs believe they can contend this season, and they have added one of the most established pitchers available to help them do it.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar has broken his silence on the growing clamour for an India recall, striking a notably measured tone even as pundits push his case for the 2027 ODI World Cup. I would tell him to do all the tournaments - first class, the Vijay Hazare - everything. And get him ready for South Africa. I think we would require him there."

Yet Bhuvneshwar, who last played for India in 2022, made clear that another cap is no longer the force driving his career. The right-armer credited his home environment for helping him move on without bitterness, having been a mainstay of India's attack for the best part of a decade before sliding out of the reckoning.

Bhuvneshwar was candid about how he has come to terms with his exclusion. Speaking on the RCB Podcast, he said, "I am at peace, and I give credit to my family. At home, we never talk about cricket. We never talk about whether I'll get back into the Indian team, why I wasn't selected, or what went wrong. That played a big role, and there is no regret."

He acknowledged the difficulty of accepting such a transition after years as a central figure. Bhuvneshwar said, "When you're a core member of a team, everyone says: 'Team comes first.' But when you're no longer in the team, naturally you feel: 'Maybe I should still be there.'"

For all that, he framed his situation as a natural part of the sport. Bhuvneshwar said, "I understand that transitions are a part of sport. I understand that generations change. I'm not the first player to experience this, and I certainly won't be the last. Family plays a big role. I am happy being where I am."

Bhuvneshwar was clear that his motivation now stems from enjoyment rather than ambition. He said, "I've already played for India. That's not something I have to achieve now. If I get another opportunity, that's great, but I've been there. Everything I'm doing now is because of my love for the game."

He added that experience had given him a deeper appreciation of the sport's well-worn wisdom. Bhuvneshwar said, "When you're young and playing for India, you say you love the game. But only now do I actually understand phrases like 'control the controllables', 'don't overthink' and 'play for the passion of the game'. I can genuinely feel those things."

His form has certainly not dipped, having finished as the second-highest wicket-taker in IPL 2026 with 28 scalps in 16 matches at an economy of 7.95, integral to another RCB title.

There is a quiet wisdom in Bhuvneshwar's response that reflects well on him. Rather than fuel the speculation or lobby for a return, he has taken the pressure off himself, and his emphasis on peace over ambition suggests a man unlikely to be destabilised by the noise around his name.

The irony is that this contentment may be exactly what makes him a viable option. A bowler with nothing to prove, playing freely and taking wickets in bulk, is often more dangerous than one straining for recognition.

Whether the selectors share Ashwin's enthusiasm remains to be seen, but Bhuvneshwar has answered the question in the only way he sensibly could, by refusing to let it define him.

title: Led by veteran coach Justin Green, WSU's running backs 'want to be great'
description: Jul. 31—When someone shouts "Kirby" during a Washington State football practice, it can get a little confusing. fullText:
Jul. 31—When someone shouts "Kirby" during a Washington State football practice, it can get a little confusing.

They might grab the attention of the big boss: first-year coach Kirby Moore, or the 5-foot-11, 207-pound bruiser of a running back known as Kirby Vorhees.

Moore said that beyond Vorhees, he does not personally know any other Kirbys.

Including Moore, Vorhees said he has only ever met two other Kirbys besides himself.

The Cougars appear to be in a promising place with two members of the exclusive Kirby club saddled up and ready to do battle in the crimson and gray.

But it did, and WSU's two other top running backs joined Vorhees to form a room led by former Montana RBs coach Justin Green — another Moore assistant with a long track record of success.

"I love how hungry they are. They want to be great," Green said of Wazzu's running backs. "In this business of college football, how things are, what kind of money is being thrown at guys. These guys want to play football more than anything else."

Vorhees was one of the most prominent Cougs to announce his intention to enter the transfer portal last December when former coach Jimmy Rogers took the same post at Iowa State.

He sat out the bowl game, then was among the first Cougs to sign a revenue-sharing agreement to return to the WSU football team.

Soon after, rising sophomore Maxwell Woods signed his name on the dotted line to return and junior Leo Pulalasi was on his way back, too.

Vorhees, who ended the regular season as WSU's No. 1 running back, said that the opportunity to play, coupled with the quality of his relationships with other returning players, sealed the deal.

Unspoken, but nonetheless relevant, is a likely significant name, image and likeness package for Vorhees and the two other prominent running backs.

Woods said that the running backs talked to each other about their future every day last winter before they each decided to return.

"We all kinda had an idea, 'We really could run this back and really do what we do and do our best to take over,'" Woods said. "I'm really grateful that we are getting another year together."

Woods said that the chance to talk with Moore around the Potato Bowl in Boise sealed the deal for his return

"I just think it was more of the trust factor," Woods said of Moore. "The numbers really don't lie. He's been an elite offensive coordinator."

With 228.3 yards per game last year, Moore's Missouri Tigers were the eighth-best rushing team in the nation.

Vorhees, WSU's leading rusher in 2025, is a prototypical east-west slasher, dialing up physicality at the point of attack, said the Cougars' running back coach Justin Green.

Woods presents similar slasher skill coupled with remarkable speed, while Pulalasi packs an advanced football sense and ability to "make football plays for the football team," Green said.

"There's no overthinking when it comes to him, which I love as far as his football talent," Green said of Pulalasi. "And that's going to help us."

Freshman Tremayne Hill and Central Washington transfer Beau Phillips could also factor into the room, Green said.

Coach Green: 'Very wise ... very detailed'

When the three backs re-signed with WSU, they had no idea who their new position coach would be. Woods said he placed his trust in Moore to get that hire right, and, as proven through April's spring game, he did.

Green, who spent the last 14 years molding all-conference running backs at Montana, joins WSU as the assistant head coach/running backs coach.

Moore said that he ran into Green on the recruiting trail in the San Diego area and was impressed by his track record of success.

"We're teachers first," Moore said. "And he's done a very, very nice job."

Green left Montana after having coached half of UM's all-time top 10 rushers, including Eli Gillman, the 2023 Jerry Rice Award winner, reserved for the best freshman in the Football Championship Subdivision.

That experience has presented itself in the way that Green teaches the game of football, Vorhees and Woods said.

"Very smart, just very, very wise and very detailed," Woods said of Green. "Very detailed with every little thing, as little as steps, even just like getting the hand-off. There's so much detail."

That detail, Woods said, has expanded his understanding of football.

Green, Vorhees said, "is the smartest running back coach (he has) been around when it comes to knowing the scheme and the entirety of football itself."

Over the course of spring camp, Woods emerged as the star of the show, breaking out into several quality runs. When fall camp fires up on Aug. 6, he could make a big push for the starting job.

That's the thing about the running back room that Green didn't have to foster, he said.

"They all have different personalities and different likes and wants," Green said. "And what I noticed, probably more than anything else, is how tight their bond is. They are very bonded. They hang out with each other, they laugh, they have a good time."

It's the kind of bond Green said he has created within his Grizzlies' RB rooms — and it was already in place at Wazzu when he arrived.

Green's father, Anthony Green, was a Pop Warner and high school football coach in San Diego.

The future coach saw how hard his father worked, raising 12 kids (Justin Green has 10 brothers and one sister) and giving his best to his players.

"When you've got a guy, as far as a coach who loves you, you're willing to run through a brick wall for them because that's how you show your love back," Green said. "Growing up with that, as far as seeing that view of the way my father (acted)."

It's Anthony's example that has propelled Justin forward to his present role as mentor, teacher and father figure.

WSU's running backs are plenty talented. The retention was just the start. In a potentially explosive scheme, WSU has the chance to reach another level in the backfield.

That starts with Green, and if successful, translates to touchdowns, first downs and broken tackles.

"No matter what I know, it's what they know. And then what are they willing to do for you," Green said. "If you want the best out of them, you've got to love them, you've got to treat them, right. You've got to treat them fair, and they will reciprocate with giving you the best that they have."

title: Virginia university didn't know of student's conviction before campus shooting, report says
description: A Virginia university missed opportunities to learn of a student's terrorism-related conviction before the man opened fire in an ROTC class in March, injuring two students and killing an Army veteran ...
fullText:
RICHMOND, Va. (AP) — A Virginia university missed opportunities to learn of a student's terrorism-related conviction before the man opened fire in an ROTC class in March, injuring two students and killing an Army veteran who fought back with "extraordinary heroism," an investigative report released Tuesday found.

The federal probation officer working with Mohamed Bailor Jalloh, who spent eight years in prison for attempting to aid the Islamic State, did not share Jalloh's criminal background with Old Dominion University, despite the serious nature of the offense, according to the report, which was produced by the law firm Cooley on behalf of the university.

Jalloh, who also died in the March attack, had attended the public university in Norfolk beginning in 2007, was suspended in 2010 and reenrolled after his early release from prison in December 2024. He was readmitted to the school in May last year.

No federal or state law enforcement agency reported his prior conviction either, the report said.

State law prohibits the university from inquiring about student criminal history before admission or readmission, according to the report. The university could have asked readmitted students to voluntarily disclose their criminal history but did not at the time, the report said.

The university "had no knowledge of the risk Jalloh posed or his federal terrorism conviction," the report said. Had officials known, it's likely they would have sought his removal from campus, it said.

"Given that Virginia law requires universities to rely on student self-disclosure, it is even more important that other law enforcement agencies ensure that information that universities need to know to safeguard their students is shared with universities. This critical failure led to tragic consequences here," the report said.

Officials with the FBI, which the report said investigated Jalloh's original offense, didn't immediately respond to emailed requests for comment about the report's findings.

Paul Arnett, the chief U.S. probation officer for Virginia's eastern district federal court, reached briefly by phone, requested questions about the report's findings in writing, which the AP provided.

Jalloh, a former member of the Virginia National Guard, was sentenced to 11 years in prison after pleading guilty in 2017 to providing material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization, the Islamic State group, according to prison records. He completed a drug treatment program that allowed him early release from federal prison.

In March this year, Jalloh entered a classroom and asked whether it was an ROTC class. After students answered affirmatively, he opened fire, according to authorities and the report.

The university's president said the report also shed new light on the "extraordinary heroism and bravery" shown by the cadets and Lt. Col. Brandon Shah, the instructor who was killed.

Authorities and cadets who were in the room said they stabbed and disarmed Jalloh, the report said.

Shah "immediately grappled with the attacker, which allowed other brave students to come to his aid and many other students to escape unharmed," the report said.

Cadets tried to save Shah's life but he died at a hospital, the report said.

Family members of Shah could not immediately be reached for comment. An Old Dominion graduate and former Army pilot, he flew hundreds of hours on combat missions before returning to the university to lead the Army ROTC battalion, according to a biography published by the university.

While the report noted that the university's police department responded "almost immediately and effectively," it also recommended improvements to the university's safety and emergency response protocols.

"The campus community has my complete assurance that we will act quickly to fully implement Cooley's recommendations as we actively work to make our campus as safe and secure as possible," university President Brian O. Hemphill said in a statement.

title: Linebacker Dante Fowler Jr. eager to make impact on Seahawks talented defense
description: For veteran linebacker Dante Fowler, Jr., the chance to join the Seattle Seahawks wasn't something he was going to pass up again. fullText:
SEATTLE (AP) — For veteran linebacker Dante Fowler, Jr., the chance to join the Seattle Seahawks wasn't something he was going to pass up again.

After finishing with three sacks and 15 total tackles with Dallas last season, Fowler signed a one-year contract with the Seahawks in May worth up to $5 million.

Fowler, the No. 3 overall draft pick by the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2015, considered signing in Seattle last year before opting to go back to the Cowboys. But after an aggressive sales pitch from Seahawks veteran and former Cowboys teammate DeMarcus Lawrence, along with a visit to the team headquarters, he knew the time was finally right.

“You can see why they won the Super Bowl, whether it's on or off the field,” Fowler said. “It’s actually pretty cool to see the camaraderie here from the top to the bottom, front office and the team. It’s a great group of guys. You come into this building happy, and you come in looking forward to going to work.”

Fowler is stepping into an enviable situation for a free agent signee, with the Seahawks returning the majority of last year’s dominant defense. Linebacker Boye Mafe (Cincinnati), safety Coby Bryant (Chicago), and cornerback Riq Woolen (Philadelphia) were the most notable losses, but the Seahawks are expected to once again be among the league's best.

Even on a defense as heralded as Seattle, a veteran presence like Fowler can still help make everyone better.

“The way he comes in, he works. I think from a football aspect, like what he’s going to bring to that room, pass rush-wise, Lord, like, he’s able to get off the rock,” linebacker Ernest Jones IV said. “He has so many moves in his bag, and it’s only going to make the guys around him better.”

Fowler was also attracted to Seattle by the presence of defensive coordinator Aden Durde, who Fowler first worked with in Atlanta in 2020 when Durde was a defensive assistant, then in Dallas when Durde coached the Cowboys’ defensive line.

Durde tried hard to recruit Fowler to Seattle last season, and Fowler is excited to once again be working with the Seahawks British-born coach.

“Just to see the way he’s grown throughout his career, and being my defensive line coach at the Cowboys to now his role as a defensive coordinator here, is very awesome,” Fowler said.

Along with Durde, Fowler is eager to continue working with Seattle’s strength and conditioning staff, which he says is the best he’s ever worked with.

Fowler credits the staff for getting him into fantastic shape, which gives him optimism that he’ll have a big year like in 2024, when he had 10 1/2 sacks and 39 tackles with Washington.

“I feel like how it felt when I played in Washington with the Commanders,” Fowler said. “I just knew I was going to have a great season just because of the work that I put in all season, and how good of a shape I was. So I feel like that.”

Head coach Mike Macdonald has already started to feel Fowler’s impact three days into training camp.

“You want to affect the quarterback, but not too much at this point," Macdonald said, “so he’s doing great. He’s getting used to how we roll here, and I think he’s enjoying his time, which is positive. Definitely seeing flashes for sure.”

While he wasn’t a member of last year’s Super Bowl-winning squad, Fowler hasn’t struggled to fit in on a Seahawks team that already has plenty of star talent on defense.

“I just fall in line and do what I’m supposed to do,” Fowler said. “They already had a great defense before we got here, and they won a Super Bowl. It was the best defense in the world last year. So my job is to just fall in line and do whatever I’ve got to do to make this defense upgrade a little bit more.”

"I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading. That's why I'm here and I can't wait to get started."

Alonso was equally swift in setting out his vision for the young Englishman, telling reporters: "In that position we needed an important player, and I'm sure there were not many better options than Morgan Rogers.

"You need players who can have that almost instant impact and I'm sure Morgan won't need much time to adapt to the club, the system and his team-mates. That was the idea, to get a top player, and Morgan is one of them."

title: Will Titans add any more players before training camp?
description: The Tennessee Titans could be looking to add more veteran talent to their roster before the 2026 season kicks off.
fullText:
It’s hard to believe that the Tennessee Titans will be on the field this week, and the 2026 season will finally be underway.

General manager Mike Borgonzi has done a masterful job at remaking the Titans roster over the offseason, and now new head coach Robert Saleh will have a chance to build them back into contenders. The big question is: Are they done adding competition to the roster?

A man named Cameron from Kentucky asked Jim Wyatt a solid question about possible additions in his weekly mailbag, and the answer was interesting.

Question: Hey Jim, do you think the Titans will add a veteran to the team heading to training camp?

Jim: Yes, at several positions along the way.

The Titans have already been active, adding defensive back Nazeeh Johnson and offensive tackle Zachary Thomas since rookies reported to the team facility on Thursday; moves that coincided with the team placing JC Latham and Amani Hooker on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. Taking Wyatt at his word, who else could be on the Titans' radar?

Looking at the players still available, two names come to mind: defensive backs Ifeatu Melifonwu and Kenny Moore. Tennessee has added some new faces to the secondary, but would definitely have room for some more competition and depth. While both of those players have different skill sets, they both have the ability to fill a role heading into the season.

title: REPORT: Browns Exploring Edge Rusher Additions Ahead of Camp
description: After the blockbuster trade of Myles Garrett, Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry is hunting for a veteran defensive end to solidify a new-look front before training camp commences.
fullText:
Training camp may be just days away for the Cleveland Browns, but the roster tweaking never stops for Executive Vice President of Football Operations Andrew Berry.

Berry already pulled off a blockbuster trade earlier this summer to send Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams for a handful of picks and on-the-rise edge rusher Jared Verse. He may be looking to bolster the position even more with training camp ramping up.

According to Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com, the Browns are apparently in the market for another edge rusher.

"The Browns are still in the market for a veteran defensive end to add to the rotation and make up for the loss of former Bills edge rusher A.J. Epenesa, who failed his physical," wrote Cabot on Sunday.

She added that Cleveland would prefer to find this mystery edge rusher before training camp commences on Wednesday, but that it may take some time to actually identify someone and sign them.

Cleveland Browns Offseason Report; Which Brown is set for breakout? | Roster rankings fair or foul? The Cleveland Browns are just two weeks away from reporting to camp and then the season will be on for the Browns. Until then, it is another conversation abo...

As Cabot noted, at one point this offseason the Browns were set to sign Buffalo Bills free agent Epenesa to a contract, but balked after being uncomfortable with something that popped up during his physical.

Several months later, the former second-round pick wound up signing a one-year deal with the Philadelphia Eagles instead.

As things stand right now, the Browns boast a pretty strong starting front four along the defensive line, headlined by the newly acquired Verse. The unit also includes veteran DT Maliek Collins, 2025, No. 5 overall pick Mason Graham and 2022 third-round pick Alex Wright.

Behind those four, though, the Browns would benefit from some additional depth for rotational purposes. Cleveland will sorely miss Garrett, for obvious reasons, but building a deeper defensive line that can collectively attempt to make up for what's lost in Garrett's absence could certainly help matters.

Of course, Verse will carry the heaviest burden to replicate as much as he can, Garrett's impact, granted nobody should expect him to be the two-time Defensive Player of the Year.

He won't have to go it alone, though, and another addition to the room will only help ease some of the pressure on him, hence why adding another veteran is of the utmost importance to Berry and company. It sounds like it's just a matter of when, rather than if, Cleveland will be adding another edge rusher to their roster.

title: Davante Adams addresses Rams nearly trading him for first time
description: The Rams nearly traded Davante Adams for A.J. Brown before deciding against it, and the veteran wideout addressed those talks for the first time.
fullText:
During the 2026 NFL offseason, the Los Angeles Rams explored potential moves to add star wide receiver A.J. Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles. In the midst of those talks, reports came out that the Rams considered trading Davante Adams in order to add Brown, which head coach Sean McVay later confirmed.

The move never materialized, and Brown would eventually be traded to the New England Patriots. If circumstances were different, there's a good chance Adams could've departed one year after joining the team.

Adams was asked by reporters on Saturday about those rumors, choosing to take the professional high road and avoid making those talks a personal gripe.

"I'm a teenager in this league now, so, I mean, you got to understand there's certain things that each team, you know, does or has to do in order to -- just from top to bottom -- it's just the way that this business goes," stated Adams.

Rams WR Davante Adams on the offseason trade rumors:

"I'm a teenager in this league now, so, I mean, you got to understand there's certain things that each team, you know, does or has to do in order to -- just from top to bottom -- it's just the way that this business goes." pic.twitter.com/YukgMbPLrP

— Benjamin Royer (@thebenroyer) July 25, 2026

While Adams would be more than justified in being angry, especially after leading the NFL in receiving touchdowns and helping Matthew Stafford win MVP, his decision to focus on the things he can control is why he remains a top player, despite his veteran status. Adams also expressed that he's happy to be back and is ready to get to work.

It's easy to see why so many within the organization hold Adams in such high regard, despite 2026 being only his second year with the franchise. Adams is entering the final year of his deal.

title: Dodgers to activate closer Edwin Díaz from IL on Wednesday after 3 months out
description: Veteran utility man Kiké Hernández will also reportedly be activated on Tuesday.
fullText:
Edwin Díaz, the most expensive closer in baseball, is about to return to the Los Angeles Dodgers. With hopefully better results this time.

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Saturday the team plans to activate Díaz on Wednesday, according to AM 570's Dave Vassegh. Veteran utility man Kiké Hernández will also reportedly be activated on Tuesday.

Díaz is currently on a rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City and is scheduled to make one more appearance on Sunday.

Díaz joined the Dodgers on a three-year, $69 million contract in free agency last winter, making him MLB's highest-paid reliever after a standout career with the New York Mets. The early returns were less than what the Dodgers would have hoped, with seven earned runs allowed in his first six innings.

At 32 years old, Díaz struggled with his control, which wasn't above average even in the best of times. After seven appearances, the Dodgers shelved him in April due to loose bodies in his elbow.

Since then, the Dodgers have leaned on a resurgent Tanner Scott as their closer, an ironic development given they only signed Díaz after Scott's struggles in his first season on a similarly large contract. Overall, the team's bullpen ranks seventh in MLB with a 3.77 ERA.

Díaz and Hernández are two of several names the Dodgers will be hoping to re-introduce in the second half, with starting pitchers Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, reliever Blake Treinen and catcher Will Smith among those waiting in the wings.

title: Ravens to sign veteran offensive lineman Hakeem Adeniji
description: Baltimore plans to sign veteran offensive lineman Hakeem Adeniji, adding a versatile blocker with 16 career starts.
fullText:
The Baltimore Ravens plan to sign veteran offensive lineman Hakeem Adeniji, according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, adding another experienced and versatile blocker to a unit that has undergone significant change this offseason.

Adeniji worked out for the Ravens before the team decided to add him. The 28-year-old has appeared in 55 regular-season games with 16 starts since entering the NFL as a sixth-round pick of the Cincinnati Bengals in 2020. He spent last season with the Dallas Cowboys, appearing in 12 games and making one start at left guard. Adeniji has also spent time with the Minnesota Vikings and Cleveland Browns.

The Ravens plan to sign veteran OL Hakeem Adeniji, per source. 

Adeniji has 16 career starts since 2029, including one with Dallas last year.

— Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) July 25, 2026

The 6-foot-4, 302-pound Adeniji offers experience at tackle and guard, giving Baltimore another option as it evaluates its offensive line combinations during training camp. He made 15 of his starts during three seasons with Cincinnati and started at right guard in Super Bowl LVI. His only start for Dallas came at left guard, where he helped the Cowboys produce 180 rushing yards despite playing without several starters, according to the Cowboys’ official website.

Adeniji does not necessarily arrive with a direct path to a starting job. His immediate value comes from his ability to provide competition and experienced depth at multiple positions. That flexibility can become particularly valuable during training camp, when injuries and shifting combinations often test the depth of an offensive line.

Baltimore has already added veteran center Ethan Pocic and brought back guard John Simpson while reshaping the group in front of Lamar Jackson. Adeniji represents another low-risk move designed to strengthen the unit’s floor.

The Ravens will still need to evaluate how much Adeniji can contribute, but his experience and positional flexibility give him a legitimate opportunity to earn a reserve role.
